trending.title: Brussels changes gear on Big Tech enforcement
trending.body: As the EU’s focus shifts from big-ticket fines to compliance, concerns are growing that the market power of dominant tech platforms could become more entrenched.

trending.title: Nigel Farage wants to scrap GDPR for the UK
trending.body: Reform UK said GDPR has “strangled small businesses and tech firms.”

trending.title: Poll: The older and richer you are, the more you like AI
trending.body: Optimism for AI increases with age and wealth, with young adults the most pessimistic, polling shared with POLITICO shows.

trending.title: How satellite technology can help Europe battle wildfires
trending.body: As summer blazes are again spreading across the continent, satellites can now gather images and data to map damage and detect fires at an early stage.

trending.title: UK ‘open to discussing’ digital services tax with Trump administration
trending.body: Jamieson Greer said Donald Trump’s threat to slap 100% tariffs on European countries with digital services taxes is “not a bluff.”

privacy.title: Flipping the kill switch: I survived 72 hours without US tech
privacy.body: The EU wants to decrease reliance on American technology. Here’s what happened when a POLITICO reporter tried to live and work without it.

regulatory.title: Von der Leyen set to deliver major speech on Europe’s space policy
regulatory.body: The speech is the first ever by the Commission president dedicated solely to space policy at a moment of heightened security concern over satellites.

regulatory.title: The US got Meta to change Instagram and Facebook. Europe wants in.
regulatory.body: The European Commission may be looking for bigger changes than Meta agreed to with 47 U.S. states.

regulatory.title: Poland asks EU to fine Meta €250 million over scam ads
regulatory.body: Polish authorities have notified Meta multiple times, but the company still hasn’t offered “an effective and adequate response” to the issue, the country’s deputy prime minister writes.

regulatory.title: Meta’s mega-deal could change the game for social media
regulatory.body: Almost all U.S. states are using litigation to impose kids’ protections that Congress failed to pass.

regulatory.title: Meta agrees to pay $17B, adopt kids’ safety features to resolve US lawsuits
regulatory.body: The tentative agreement is a massive concession from the tech giant.

regulatory.title: Andy Burnham has to shape the UK’s social media ban. Australia and France could show him how.
regulatory.body: The U.K. can learn from Australia and France’s attempts to kick kids off social media.

regulatory.title: The trade war came too soon for Mark Carney’s middle powers alliance
regulatory.body: The Canadian prime minister called for pro-trade democracies to resist great-power coercion together. Seven months later, he is largely fighting Trump alone.

regulatory.title: UN chief tells countries to rein in autonomous weapons
regulatory.body: Countries are set to gather in November for talks on weapons which use AI.

regulatory.title: Waymo to launch robotaxis in Munich in 2027
regulatory.body: The news marks the self-driving taxi company’s first foray into the European Union.

regulatory.title: How a 17th-century Irish law is shielding Big Tech from class actions in Europe
regulatory.body: Ireland has limits on outside funding for court challenges, stopping Europeans from seeking compensation from Big Tech for harms.

regulatory.title: LAYING THE GROUNDWORK FOR AI-POWERED CYBERSECURITY
regulatory.body: The EU’s Action Plan on Cybersecurity and AI lays the groundwork for new, AI-powered approaches to IT security but organizations need to ensure their security foundations are fit for purpose.

regulatory.title: Parents and politicians love social media bans for kids. Experts worry they’re a shot in the dark.
regulatory.body: The science behind kicking kids off social media is murky at best, and experts say it could backfire.

regulatory.title: EU moves to ease subsidy rules for small media
regulatory.body: Revised state aid rules prioritize SMEs, innovation and social inclusion.

regulatory.title: Greece sabotages its own plans to reverse the brain drain of scientists
regulatory.body: Athens is trying to lure back researchers after an exodus during the financial crisis, but a major EU-backed scheme has fallen apart.

regulatory.title: From factory to front lines: A Western spy drone’s journey to war in Ukraine
regulatory.body: Drones have transformed the war in Ukraine, and AR3 unmanned aircraft from Portuguese company Tekever are playing a key role.

regulatory.title: French court blocks social media ban for under 15s
regulatory.body: Ruling could have far-reaching implications about kids’ rights to access the internet.

regulatory.title: US lawmakers visit Vatican to discuss AI — and meet the pope
regulatory.body: The visit comes as the Catholic Church, including Pope Leo XIV, has increasingly focused on the rapidly developing technology.
